newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money ends up, security prices weaken.
newsitem.headline: India call money ends up, security prices weaken.

text.p: Indian call money closed lower on Monday at eight percent against the opening levels of 8.0-8.75 percent and dealers said they expected rates to come down further during the week.
They said call money rates were likely to ease as the reporting day approached. Banks report their positions to the Reserve Bank of India on Friday.

"A fall in rates is usual in the second half of a reporting fortnight," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Many banks seem to have covered their positions already and we expect call money to drop lower as the week progresses."
Dealers said secondary market prices of government securities fell in light trade.

"Some market players are uncertain about call money," said a dealer. "With rates remaining around eight percent for more than three days now, they have decided to sell securities at whatever price is available."
The selling pressure was dragging prices down, he said.
Dealers said the 13.70 percent 1999 government of India stock traded at 100.95 rupees and the 13.62 percent at 102.75.
Treasury bills maturing in March 1997 yielded 8.10 percent and bills maturing in June 1997 yielded 9.85 percent, they said.
